name:
Example: 
                    Finding a Correlation Coefficient Given Variances and Covariance
problem: The variances of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are $25$ and $36,$ respectively. Given that $\textrm{Cov}[X,Y] = 18,$ find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$
worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}[X, Y] }{\textrm {SD}[X] \cdot \textrm {SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\textrm{Cov}[X, Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\textrm {SD}[X]$ and $\textrm {SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{25}=5, \\ \text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[Y]}=\sqrt{36}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting our data in the formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[X]} \\  & =\frac{18}{5\cdot 6} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
